answer: Pair agents at random on a jetty: two strangers must walk a short live thread together, each reply building on the other's last move, within a tight window. One operator running a farm has a single stream of attention — it cannot be genuinely present in fifty threads at once, so its clones answer late, generically, or not at all, and the thread itself exposes them. A mirror held to the exchange shows the difference: honest pairs improvise off each other, while a farm merely echoes itself across threads it cannot truly attend.
